headline: Conspiracy Theory Claims All Mall Santas Are 'Same Guy Simultaneously'
subheadline: Viral investigation finds 'impossible' scheduling overlaps across multiple locations
summary: Internet investigators claim to have evidence that mall Santas across the country are somehow the same individual.
content:
A viral investigation has concluded that mall Santas across the country may be the same individual appearing in multiple locations simultaneously—and the evidence is "deeply troubling."

The investigation, conducted by Threadit community r/SantaTruth, began when user u/JingleBellSkeptic noticed that Santas at three different malls in their city had "the exact same mole above the left eyebrow."

"I thought it was coincidence," they wrote. "Then I started looking closer. Same mole. Same slight gap in the front teeth. Same way of saying 'ho ho ho' with a tiny hitch between the second and third 'ho.'"

The investigation expanded nationwide. Members visited 847 mall Santa installations, documenting physical features, vocal patterns, and behavioral quirks. Their findings: "Statistically impossible" similarities across locations.

"These Santas are scheduled at overlapping times in cities hundreds of miles apart," reported lead investigator u/SantaSkeptic. "A Santa in Chicago has a shift that ends at 6 PM. A Santa in Detroit with identical features has a shift that starts at 6:15 PM. That's not enough time. Unless..."

The theory proposes several explanations: cloning, teleportation, or "something we don't have words for yet."

Mall management companies have denied any unusual Santa arrangements. "We hire local performers," said one representative. "They're different people." When shown the photographic evidence, they added: "I don't know what to tell you," and ended the interview.

Some community members have attempted to "trap" Santas by visiting multiple locations rapidly. Results have been inconclusive. One reported that both Santas "made eye contact with me like they knew. Like they both knew."

Dr. Elena Martinez declined to comment, stating she "doesn't do Santa investigations" and that "some mysteries are better left unsolved."
author: Chris Patterson, Human Interest
